ds: Inherent-risk factors relating to who the customer is and how they behave towards the institution. Covers politically exposed persons, non-residents, cash-intensive businesses, complex structures, reluctance to provide information and negative news. Used as the customer-risk dimension of an enterprise-wide or customer risk assessment.

src.t: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach (sector-specific guidance series, general principles)
FATF Recommendations, Recommendation 1 and Interpretive Note (assessing risks and applying a risk-based approach)
Wolfsberg Group, Guidance on a Risk Based Approach for Managing Money Laundering Risks (2006)

cn.rt: Cross-cutting risk factor; applies across all consumer products and channels. Customer type risk such as PEPs and non-residents.

rat: Generic customer-type risk: PEPs, non-residents, cash-intensive and complex-structure customers.

ind.n: Politically exposed person as customer or controller
ind.cx: The customer, a beneficial owner or a controller is a domestic or foreign PEP, or a family member or close associate of one.
ind.fp: Many PEPs, particularly domestic or low-level officials, are lawfully wealthy and low risk once source of wealth is understood.
ind.ds: The customer, a beneficial owner or a controller is a domestic or foreign PEP, or a family member or close associate of one.

ind.cx: Customer resides outside the institution's market and cannot explain why they need an account or service here.
ind.fp: Expatriates, students, property investors and cross-border workers often have legitimate need.
ind.ds: Customer resides outside the institution's market and cannot explain why they need an account or service here.

ind.cx: Customer's business model relies heavily on cash receipts (e.g. retail, restaurants, car washes, vending), making revenue hard to verify.
ind.fp: Cash-heavy trades are common and legitimate; indicator only grows with volume out of line with peers.
ind.ds: Customer's business relies heavily on cash receipts, making revenue difficult to verify against stock, costs or card use.

ind.cx: Customer is part of a multi-layer or multi-jurisdiction structure without an evident commercial purpose.
ind.fp: Large groups, funds and tax-efficient structures can be complex for lawful reasons.
ind.ds: Multiple tiers of entities, trusts or foundations, often across secrecy or low-transparency jurisdictions, with no evident business or tax reason.
ind.cn: Complex layered structure without commercial rationale

ind.n: Unwillingness or inability to provide information
ind.cx: Customer delays, refuses or gives evasive answers to KYC or refresh requests, or withdraws when questioned.
ind.fp: Customers may be privacy-conscious, unfamiliar with requirements or have genuinely lost documents.
ind.ds: Customer or counterparty delays, refuses or gives incomplete or evasive responses to KYC, refresh or request-for-information enquiries.
ind.cn: Refusal or delay in answering due diligence requests

ind.n: Adverse media on customer or associates
ind.cx: Credible negative news links the customer or associated parties to financial crime, corruption or regulatory action.
ind.fp: Name matches, old or unproven allegations and unrelated namesakes are common.
ind.ds: Credible negative news, enforcement notices or investigations link the customer, its owners or associates to criminal, corrupt or regulated-sector misconduct.

ind.n: Customer reluctant to disclose beneficial owner or purpose
ind.cx: Customer is vague about who ultimately benefits from the account or the intended use of funds.
ind.fp: Trustees, professionals and privacy-sensitive clients may need time to supply details.
ind.ds: Customer or intermediary is vague, delayed or inconsistent when asked who owns, controls or ultimately benefits from an account, entity or funds.
ind.cn: Reluctance to disclose beneficial ownership or control

ind.n: Customer with prior regulatory, criminal or sanctions history
ind.cx: Customer or principal has previous convictions, enforcement action, or has been exited by another institution.
ind.fp: Spent or unrelated histories may not indicate current risk.
ind.ds: Customer or principal has previous convictions, enforcement or disciplinary action, or has been exited by another institution.
ind.cn: Prior regulatory, criminal or enforcement history

ind.n: Occupation or business inconsistent with wealth
ind.cx: Declared occupation, age or business does not plausibly explain the scale of assets or funds.
ind.fp: Inheritance, windfalls or undeclared secondary income can explain gaps.
ind.ds: Declared occupation, age or business does not plausibly explain the scale of assets or funds.

ind.cx: Customer operates in a sector with elevated misuse risk, such as precious metals, gambling, crypto, arms, or money transfer.
ind.fp: Most firms in these sectors are regulated and compliant.
ind.ds: Customer operates in a sector with elevated misuse risk, such as precious metals, gambling, crypto, arms, or money transfer.

ind.cx: Customer repeatedly changes name, address, contact, signatories or ownership shortly after onboarding.
ind.fp: Life events, relocations and restructures legitimately change details.
ind.ds: Customer or entity repeatedly changes name, address, contact details, directors, signatories or ownership.
ind.cn: Frequent changes of customer or entity details

ctl.ds: Applies corroborated source-of-wealth checks, senior sign-off, enhanced monitoring and sceptical review of public-sector links for politically exposed persons and their networks. It targets the corruption and misappropriation risk specific to these customers.

ctl.n: PEP, relative and close associate screening
ctl.ds: Screens customers, beneficial owners, controllers, counterparties and their relatives and close associates against politically exposed person data at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. Matches trigger enhanced measures and senior approval.

Assigns each customer a risk tier from factors such as customer type, sector, geography, products and channel, which then drives the depth of due diligence and monitoring. Consistent scoring focuses resources on higher-risk relationships.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.

ctl.n: Cash deposit profiling and peer benchmarking
ctl.ds: Compares cash deposits and withdrawals with expected activity, sector and location peers and declared turnover, alerting on outliers. It helps find cash that is inconsistent with the stated business.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

Requires a documented commercial or legal reason for each layer of a multi-tier or cross-border structure, with specialist review and sign-off before approval. Unexplained complexity is treated as a risk driver and can lead to decline.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.

ctl.n: Account restriction, decline and exit policy
ctl.ds: Defines when a relationship or supplier must be declined, restricted or terminated, for example for unresolved due diligence, non-cooperation or unmanageable risk, with timelines and approvers. It prevents indefinite continuation of relationships that cannot be controlled.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

ctl.n: Alert adjudication standards and quality assurance
ctl.ds: Defines documented criteria for clearing or escalating screening and monitoring alerts, resolves matches using secondary identifiers and samples closed alerts for quality. It makes decisions consistent, defensible and auditable.

Prevents account opening or activity until ownership and control information is provided and verified, with refusals escalated to compliance and unresolved cases handled under a defined policy. It stops relationships starting on withheld or unresolved ownership.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.

ctl.n: Duplicate and synthetic identity checks at onboarding
ctl.ds: Compares new applicant identifiers such as name, email, phone, address, device and bank account with existing customers, previously declined or exited applicants and known-bad data. Matches are blocked or referred, limiting repeat applicants, synthetic identities and mule recruitment.

ctl.n: Senior management approval and risk acceptance
ctl.ds: Requires named senior management or a committee to approve onboarding, continuation or waivers for higher-risk relationships, with documented mitigations and periodic re-approval. It adds accountability and an independent challenge to risk acceptance.

Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.

Establishes how a customer accumulated their overall wealth and corroborates it with independent evidence rather than relying on self-declaration. It is central to managing high-net-worth, politically exposed and high-value-purchase relationships.

Verifies licences, registrations and supervisory status of customers, agents and counterparties against regulator registers before onboarding and periodically. It confirms legal authority to operate and detects unlicensed activity.

ctl.n: Account detail change monitoring and cool-down
ctl.ds: Contact, device or payee changes trigger notification to the prior channel and restrict risky actions for a short period, with alerts on clusters of changes. It disrupts takeover.
